content:
The [Average Calculator](/average-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Mean, median, mode and range of a list. Enter your numbers (comma or space separated) and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

The average (arithmetic mean) is the sum of values divided by how many there are. Median and mode give a fuller picture when data has outliers. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers. Related Math tools include [Percentage Calculator](/percentage-calculator), [Fraction Calculator](/fraction-calculator) and [Square Root Calculator](/square-root-calculator).

## How to use the Average Calculator

Start by typing or pasting your numbers (comma or space separated). The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults. The steps below walk through each input in order.

1. Type or paste your numbers (comma or space separated).
2. Check the result — it updates instantly as you type.
3. Use Reset to start over with the default values.

## Formula

Mean = Σx ÷ n. Median = middle value of the sorted list. Mode = most frequent value.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Average Calculator](/average-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic. If the figures look wrong, check your inputs first — a misplaced decimal point is the usual culprit.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. For 4, 8, 8, 15, 16, 23, 42: mean 16.57, median 15, mode 8, range 38. Try the same figures in the [Average Calculator](/average-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves. The steps are the same whatever numbers you use; only the figures change.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Numbers (comma or space separated): 4, 8, 15, 16, 23, 42, 8), the [Average Calculator](/average-calculator) returns Mean (average): 16.5714, Median: 15, Mode: 8, Range: 38, Count / Sum: 7 / 116. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. Change any value and every figure updates instantly. ## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Use the median for skewed data like house prices.
- One extreme outlier can pull the mean a long way.

Keep these in mind and the figures will be as useful as the numbers you put in.

## Frequently asked questions

### Mean vs median — which is better?

The median resists outliers; the mean uses every value. Use both for skewed data. Try it with your own numbers in the [Average Calculator](/average-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Can there be more than one mode?

Yes — data can be bimodal or multimodal. Try it with your own numbers in the [Average Calculator](/average-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the Average Calculator use?

Mean = Σx ÷ n. Median = middle value of the sorted list. Mode = most frequent value. You can see it in action in the [Average Calculator](/average-calculator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.

### What do I need to use the Average Calculator?

Just Numbers (comma or space separated). Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
